architecture_axes.meaning: Implements explicitly granted host facilities behind opaque effect and resource contracts.
Owns process and application lifecycle in a browser, native process, test process, or another embedding.
Selects one coherent runtime, host, renderer, capability provider, server adapter, and shell composition.
Lowers the semantic UI tree to DOM, native controls, a custom scene, or deterministic headless output.
Executes eligible Elixir or BEAM logic through ERTS, AtomVM, AtomVM-in-Wasm, or another declared runtime.
Connects portable browser behavior to Phoenix, Plug, another transport, or no remote server.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: All 290 source claims retain reciprocal owned acceptance conditions and zero executed evidence.
reconciliation_checks.method: Run the Phase 5 validator and compare locked source-kind, family, milestone, profile, budget, and gate counts.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Standalone DOM, LiveView DOM adaptation, Phoenix, Plug, headless, browser host, and runtime responsibilities remain separate.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare ADR ownership tables, repository package indexes, profile compositions, and prohibited dependency statements.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Runtime substrate, execution host, renderer backend, capability provider, server adapter, and profile composition remain independent terms.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare canonical definitions, forbidden equivalences, ADR decisions, roadmap language, and repository root architecture text.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Portable components use semantic effects and opaque resources without receiving browser, operating-system, or toolkit provider objects.
reconciliation_checks.method: Inspect capability ownership, forbidden portable tokens, cleanup policy, and all classified capability references.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: The locked MudBlazor reference maps to exactly 83 normalized BlazeX families and twelve reviewed exception records.
reconciliation_checks.method: Run catalog and classification validators, generators, source-identity closure, and exception coverage checks.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Every family has disposition, tier, package, capability, remote, fallback, portability, native, visual, rationale, and future evidence gates.
reconciliation_checks.method: Validate all 83 complete classification records, locked counts, dependency graph, fallback matrix, and evidence-state prohibitions.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Catalog, classification, and acceptance generated views are deterministic and fresh relative to their authored sources.
reconciliation_checks.method: Run every generator in check mode and perform independent two-output acceptance generation comparison.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: The headless profile has no browser, DOM, Phoenix, Plug, or native-toolkit dependency and remains a deterministic conformance composition.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare profile capability and forbidden-dependency records with package and integration scaffold responsibilities.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Browser and headless planning do not imply desktop, native-host, native-control, WebView, or standalone-Wasm support.
reconciliation_checks.method: Inspect forbidden claims, non-goals, native-spike gate, backend coverage states, and acceptance prohibited results.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: No contract promises .NET, Razor, Blazor binary, MudBlazor API, NuGet, package, or renderer compatibility.
reconciliation_checks.method: Inspect explicit non-goals, family prohibited results, compatibility ADR, generated reports, and release language.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: All eighteen scaffold packages have one bounded responsibility and preserve inward dependency direction toward host-neutral contracts.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare package directories and README boundaries with the ownership map and classified component package assignments.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: The Plug package/profile excludes Phoenix, LiveView, LocalLiveView, and the LiveView DOM adapter transitively.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare Plug exclusions, profile composition, server adapter ownership, DOM renderer boundary, and acceptance coverage.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Source pins, generated outputs, adapted material, assets, dependencies, notices, and licenses have explicit future blocking gates.
reconciliation_checks.method: Inspect source hashes, catalog reference lock linkage, provenance gate requirements, evidence policy, and non-waivable release outcomes.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Thirty-one budgets, eight failure scenarios, seven blockers, and twenty-one gate requirements remain complete and explicitly unexecuted.
reconciliation_checks.method: Run quality validation and compare dimensions, environments, methods, owners, first milestones, evidence states, and budget acceptance links.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Portable component and semantic-tree contracts contain no HTML, CSS, DOM, JavaScript, LiveView, Phoenix, or native-toolkit objects.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare kernel/tree/renderer decisions and run forbidden portable-token classification validation.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: Browser code and state remain untrusted while authority-bearing Phoenix and Plug commands require server revalidation and authorization.
reconciliation_checks.method: Compare trust boundaries, security invariants, command gate requirements, CSRF/origin policy, and fallback outcomes.

reconciliation_checks.assertion: All browser, runtime, toolchain, profile, implementation, measurement, and release support remains candidate or unsupported until later evidence executes.
reconciliation_checks.method: Inspect support vocabularies, current browser statuses, evidence states, acceptance status combinations, and prohibited false-support transitions.

reviews.independence: A separate evidence-first accessibility lens challenged source-bound claims after reconciliation and did not treat phase completion as approval.
A separate architecture lens re-derived package, adapter, profile, and backend boundaries from bound sources rather than trusting prior summaries.
A separate implementation lens attempted to falsify feasibility assumptions using only current evidence states and scaffold contents, not intended architecture.
A separate packaging lens compared all eighteen package responsibilities and payload ownership to future artifact and dependency obligations.
A separate quantitative lens checked every proposed threshold, method, environment, failure bound, and blocker without interpreting proposals as measurements.
A separate product lens reviewed bounded promises, omissions, family dispositions, fallback language, and support states from a consumer perspective.
A separate provenance lens checked immutable source bindings, generator ownership, licensing boundaries, and future distributed-material gates.
A separate security lens challenged client trust, command authority, capability grants, request boundaries, deployment controls, and diagnostics.

findings.statement: The semantic and fallback contract is complete, but no browser, assistive-technology, keyboard, touch, forced-color, zoom, reflow, or reduced-motion evidence has executed.
findings.required_action: Execute renderer-normalized automated checks and bounded manual matrices as each implementation milestone introduces supported behavior.

findings.statement: The public design excludes browser objects, but only the BH-02 headless, DOM, and disposable native-control trace can expose implementation-time leakage.
findings.required_action: Run the same bounded semantic interaction traces across headless, DOM, and actual native controls before stabilizing portable contracts.

findings.statement: No clean-machine Popcorn and AtomVM browser build, nested-state behavior, authenticated server command, emitted artifact, or runtime limitation has been reproduced.
findings.required_action: Execute the pinned BH-01 feasibility matrix and stop before framework abstraction if the exact candidate composition cannot reproduce.

findings.statement: Package boundaries and payload ownership are defined, but no dependency graph, client reachability, manifest, integrity, lockfile, or artifact accounting exists.
findings.required_action: Establish deterministic reachability and manifest evidence before client-safe package or production payload claims are made.

findings.statement: All 31 thresholds are proposed and method-complete but remain empirically uncalibrated on exact desktop, mobile, browser, network, cache, and power environments.
findings.required_action: Measure the BH-01 baseline on fingerprinted environments and propose versioned threshold changes rather than claiming a pass from estimates.

findings.statement: The browser, runtime, toolchain, profile, and rendering-mode promises are bounded, but every browser configuration and implementation state remains unsupported or unproven.
findings.required_action: Qualify exact candidate versions and scenarios in BH-01 and preserve unsupported status for every untested combination.

findings.statement: Research source pins are governed, but no future distributed dependency, adapted code, generated code, icon, font, style, example, SBOM, or notice bundle has been audited.
findings.required_action: Attach complete source, license, notice, integrity, transformation, and reachability records as implementation and packaging artifacts are introduced.

findings.statement: Trust, authority, capability, CSRF/origin, integrity, CSP, dependency, secret, and redaction requirements are explicit but have no executable implementation evidence.
findings.required_action: Exercise one authenticated and authorized command boundary in BH-01, then implement the complete security gate in owning milestones.

risks.statement: The candidate browser runtime may not support a practical authenticated Phoenix command and result path without unsafe coupling or unavailable APIs.
risks.stop_condition: Stop if server authority cannot remain independent of client presentation and private renderer state.

risks.statement: Cross-origin isolation, worker, module, memory, or other browser prerequisites may narrow the candidate support window or break fallback behavior.
risks.stop_condition: Stop support promotion when prerequisites cannot be detected and failed with intentional accessible fallback.

risks.statement: The exact Popcorn, LocalLiveView, or related candidate dependency set may be private, unavailable, unlicensed for distribution, or operationally unstable.
risks.stop_condition: Stop if a required dependency cannot be reproducibly acquired and legally/operationally used by a clean environment.

risks.statement: AtomVM-in-Wasm transfer, startup, memory, interaction, and battery behavior may exceed the proposed constrained-mobile quality boundaries.
risks.stop_condition: Stop abstraction work if representative mobile results are outside a product-viable range without a bounded mitigation path.

risks.statement: LocalLiveView or LiveView render-data and patch integration may depend on private/version-sensitive APIs too broad to isolate sustainably.
risks.stop_condition: Stop the adapter path if coupling escapes the dedicated package or cannot be pinned and characterized precisely.

risks.statement: The candidate AtomVM browser runtime may lack process, timer, message, module, error, or resource semantics needed by representative component behavior.
risks.stop_condition: Stop when a required semantic cannot be reproduced or safely replaced without redefining the component contract.

risks.statement: Exact Erlang, Elixir, AtomVM, Popcorn, Phoenix, LiveView, and JavaScript tool versions may not produce a deterministic clean-machine build.
risks.stop_condition: Stop if immutable inputs and documented commands cannot reproduce equivalent browser artifacts on a clean machine.

risks.statement: The emitted Wasm, bytecode, JavaScript, assets, source maps, and transitive runtime content may be too opaque for payload and provenance accounting.
risks.stop_condition: Stop support or packaging claims when artifact origin, reachability, integrity, licensing, or payload cannot be explained.
